items.title: Muhoozi cancels $3bn Turkish SGR contract linking Uganda to Kenya
items.description: Uganda's military chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba announced the cancellation of a $3 billion SGR contract with Turkish firm Yapi Merkezi and called for protests at the Turkish Embassy, before later reversing the decision on President Museveni's instructions.
content: NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 21 – Uganda’s Chief of Defence Forces General Muhoozi Kainerugaba has announced the cancellation of a multi-billion-dollar contract awarded to Turkish construction firm Yapi Merkezi to build the country’s Standard Gauge Railway (SGR), throwing the future of the regional infrastructure project into uncertainty.
Muhoozi, the son of President Yoweri Museveni, said Uganda would seek another contractor to undertake the railway project, which is expected to connect Kampala to Malaba on the Kenyan border.
In a series of posts on X , the military chief declared that the government had terminated the agreement with the Turkish company, without providing details of the circumstances behind the decision.
“We have cancelled the contract with the Turkish company to build the SGR. We will get another one that is more worthy of our country!” he wrote.
He also called on supporters of the Patriotic League of Uganda (PLU), a political organisation he chairs, to organise demonstrations outside the Turkish Embassy in Kampala on June 19.

From “All Politicians Must Go” to Defending Political Godfathers....How Kenya’s Youth Lost Control of Their Own Movement
items.description: One thing young Kenyans need to confront is how quickly the goalposts have shifted since the 2024 protests. We went from “All Politicians Must Go” to watching the same old...
content: One thing young Kenyans need to confront is how quickly the goalposts have shifted since the 2024 protests. We went from “All Politicians Must Go” to watching the same old politicians dominate political conversations, with young people now fighting over personalities they once rejected.
At what point did the generation that rejected political godfathers become so emotionally attached to those same politicians that questioning them is now considered betrayal?

What happened to the demands for accountability, an end to corruption, reduced government spending and a complete change in how this country is governed? How did we move from rejecting the entire political establishment to defending individual politicians as though they were sent from heaven?

Some young people have become so politically naive that they genuinely believe a candidate surrounded by wealthy political families, powerful establishment figures and people associated with past public finance controversies must automatically have their interests at heart.

We spent years questioning the handling of Eurobond proceeds, the accumulation of unexplained wealth and the political families that have enjoyed enormous influence while ordinary Kenyans struggle to survive. Yet today, some young people barely question the same political networks when they appear behind their preferred candidates.

How does a politician become a symbol of change simply because they have joined the side you support? Does yesterday's political baggage disappear because someone has endorsed your favourite candidate?

The real question is who is setting the agenda today. Is it the young people who started the movement, or the legacy politicians who already control political parties, campaign financing, grassroots networks and the machinery of electoral politics?

Having thousands of people on X Spaces, trending hashtags and making noise online is not the same as controlling a political movement. You can dominate social media for an entire week while someone else makes all the important political decisions.

And any young person who confidently tells you that “We are in control” should explain exactly what decisions young people are making independently of the established political class. Otherwise, they are simply selling you Coke.

What makes this particularly interesting is how quickly the standards change depending on which politician is involved. The corruption that was unacceptable yesterday suddenly becomes a secondary issue when the accused politician joins the preferred political camp.

The 2024 protests were bigger than Ruto, bigger than the opposition and bigger than any political family. They raised fundamental questions about how Kenya is governed, how public money is spent and why ordinary citizens must keep paying for the failures of successive administrations.
Those questions should not disappear because the country is approaching another election.
The most uncomfortable question remains unanswered. Did the political establishment actually change, or did some of the young people who wanted to dismantle it simply find new politicians to defend?

Mudavadi Rallies Western Kenya Behind Ruto as Govt Unveils Multi-Billion Projects
items.description: Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi exuded confidence that President Ruto would secure a second term in a free and fair election, declaring his full support

Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi has called on residents of Western Kenya to throw their full support behind President William Ruto ahead of the next general election, arguing that political opposition has historically failed to deliver tangible development to the region.

Speaking in Butere on Friday, November 20, Mudavadi invoked the legacy of the late Martin Shikuku, widely regarded as a standard-bearer of opposition politics in Western Kenya , to make his case that opposition politics cannot be a permanent destination for the region's leaders.

The Prime Cabinet Secretary went further to predict that Ruto would secure a second term in a free and fair election, declaring his full commitment to the partnership with the President.

President Ruto, also speaking at rallies in the region, announced a sweeping package of government investments for Kakamega County under the affordable housing programme. He said the government had committed KSh 21 billion to construct housing units, hostels, and markets across the county.

Specifically, the President said 850 housing units are under construction in Kakamega, alongside a planned 14-storey building and an additional 2,000 units to be built in the area. He added that 20 markets are either complete or ongoing in the county.
Ruto also announced a KSh 3 billion allocation from the Housing Fund to construct hostels for 11,000 university students in Kakamega, with hostels to be built within every constituency.

The Sacco Societies Regulatory Authority (SASRA) has published its SACCO Supervision Annual Report 2025 , released on October 6, ranking Kenya's Deposit-Taking Saccos (DT-Saccos) across a range of financial health indicators.
PAY ATTENTION: TUKO is in WhatsApp Channels now! Subscribe and read news in your favourite messenger.

The report measures five core metrics: Core Capital to Total Assets (CCA), Core Capital to Total Deposits (CCD), Institutional Capital to Total Assets (ICA), external borrowing levels, and Non-Performing Loan (NPL) ratios. Based on these indicators, the following ten institutions stand out as the most financially stable.
Winas DT-Sacco leads the rankings, posting a CCD ratio of 84.94% against the regulatory minimum of 8%, alongside a CCA of 42.22%, zero external borrowing, and an NPL ratio of just 1.61%.

Kenya National Police (KNP) DT-Sacco, the third-largest by total assets, follows closely with a CCA of 35.67%, an ICA of 30.11%, no external debt, and an NPL of 2.33%.
Transnation DT-Sacco ranks third, meeting all capital thresholds comfortably with a CCA of 21.10% and an NPL of 2.90%, while Hazina DT-Sacco records a CCA of 16.15% and an NPL ratio of just 2.00%.
Sheria DT-Sacco, which serves Kenya's legal fraternity, maintains a CCA of 18.17% and zero external borrowing, with NPLs at 2.80%.
Newfortis DT-Sacco distinguishes itself with the lowest NPL ratio on the entire list at 0.48%, supported by a CCA of 13.48% and no external debt.
Imarisha DT-Sacco records a CCA of 17.49% and an NPL of 1.53%, with minimal external borrowing of 2.44%.

Mwalimu National DT-Sacco, the largest Sacco in Kenya by total assets, improved its NPL ratio to 2.42% in 2025, reinforcing confidence in the teachers' institution. Its CCA stands at 13.96% and ICA at 9.89%.
Stima DT-Sacco, the second-largest, holds a CCA of 19.22% and an ICA of 12.84%.
KCB’s KSh 58.6b profit: What it means for your loan, hustle, job prospects
Its NPL ratio of 6.48% is higher than others on the list, though the institution carries negligible external borrowing at 1.39%.
Unison DT-Sacco rounds out the top ten with a CCA of 16.15%, zero external debt, and an NPL of 2.16%.
A consistent pattern across the top performers is the near-total absence of external borrowing, with most institutions relying entirely on member deposits.
The report also highlights that NPL ratios below 3% serve as a reliable indicator of responsible lending practices.

SASRA's data further underscores that financial stability does not correlate directly with size, as smaller institutions such as Winas and Newfortis outperform some of the sector's largest players on key capital and asset-quality metrics.
SASRA warned that SACCO members should look beyond high dividends and consider their institution’s financial health .
The regulator cautioned that excessive payouts could weaken a SACCO’s ability to lend, withstand unexpected losses and protect members’ savings.

items.title: Govt urges cooperative societies to embrace reforms to drive growth
items.description: The government has called on cooperative societies across the country to embrace reforms, digitalisation, professional management and innovation to strengthen
content: The government has called on cooperative societies across the country to embrace reforms, digitalisation, professional management and innovation to strengthen their contribution to Kenya’s economic growth and wealth creation.

Principal Secretary (PS) for the State Department for Cooperatives, Patrick Kilemi, said cooperatives must move beyond traditional savings mobilisation and agricultural produce aggregation to become commercially competitive enterprises capable of investing, processing, manufacturing and accessing local and international markets.

Speaking during the Fifth Annual Cabinet Secretary’s Consultative Forum for Cooperatives and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) held from November 16 to 20, 2026, at Sawela Lodge in Naivasha, Kilemi said cooperatives were central to the government’s Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA).

He noted that the cooperative movement had the membership base, reach and institutional capacity to mobilise domestic resources, attract investment, create employment, promote financial inclusion and connect millions of Kenyans to economic opportunities.

Kilemi challenged cooperative leaders to rethink their business models and embrace modern approaches that would enhance productivity, competitiveness and sustainability. In his view, the success of the cooperative movement should not be measured by the number of registered societies but by the economic value they create and the impact they have on the lives of their members.

Kilemi said significant progress had been made on the Cooperatives Bill, 2024, which is expected to strengthen governance, accountability and supervision within the sector. Preparatory work on the regulations required to support its implementation is also underway.
The hidden profit gap facing Kenya’s women in agribusiness

In the Saccos subsector, the government is advancing proposals for a Central Liquidity Facility and shared services framework aimed at strengthening financial stability, institutional resilience and operational efficiency.

Furthermore, the Kenya Cooperative Transformation Strategy has progressed, with its first draft undergoing stakeholder consultations to provide a long-term roadmap for modernising and improving the competitiveness of cooperative enterprises.

On digital transformation, Kilemi said the implementation of the Cooperative Management Information System was at an advanced stage, adding that the system would improve transparency, accountability, data management, registration and supervision of cooperative societies.

In the agricultural sector, the government continues to position cooperatives at the centre of strategic value chains, including coffee, dairy, livestock and cotton, with emphasis on increasing production, processing, value addition and market access.

Kilemi emphasised that the ongoing reforms were not intended merely to improve the administration of cooperative societies but to fundamentally change how they conduct business and contribute to the national economy.

The PS urged cooperative leaders and members to view the reforms as opportunities to address longstanding institutional weaknesses, strengthen their organisations and unlock new economic opportunities.

He called on cooperatives to invest in modern processing facilities, develop their own brands, establish strategic partnerships and explore international markets to ensure members benefit from greater value addition.
Saccos were also challenged to embrace technology, strengthen their financial systems and expand their role in supporting enterprise development through competitive financial services.
According to Kilemi, professionalisation, digitalisation, good governance, innovation and strategic partnerships would be critical in building strong and sustainable cooperative institutions.
Kilemi reaffirmed the government’s commitment to creating an enabling policy, legal and institutional environment to support the transformation of the cooperative movement.
He urged cooperative leaders to take ownership of the reform agenda and work closely with the government and development partners to reposition the sector as a major driver of economic growth.

Besides, he noted that the cooperative movement had played a significant role in Kenya’s economic development for generations but needed to adopt greater ambition, innovation and competitiveness to remain relevant in the changing business environment.
Station wagon registrations drop 17.2pc in Kenya

The Principal Secretary called on stakeholders to work collectively in implementing the reforms, stressing that the future of the sector would depend on their willingness to embrace change and move beyond traditional business practices.
Finally, he urged the cooperative movement to actively participate in shaping the country’s economic future rather than remain spectators to the ongoing transformation.

The forum brought together stakeholders in the cooperative and MSME sectors to deliberate on reforms, challenges and opportunities for strengthening the sectors’ contribution to Kenya’s economic transformation.

items.title: Australia Introduces New Mandatory Visa Law Banning Visitors From Visa Hopping From November 28
items.description: Australia will impose Condition 8503 on visitor visa holders from 28 November 2026, blocking switches to work, student and partner visas while in Australia.
content: PAY ATTENTION: Mark TUKO.co.ke as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed!

Elijah Ntongai is an experienced editor at TUKO.co.ke, with more than four years in financial, business, labour and technology reporting. His work provides valuable insights into Kenyan, African, and global trends
Australia will enforce a sweeping immigration restriction from November 28, 2026, barring most visitor visa holders from applying to switch to other visa categories while remaining in the country.

The changes were formalised through the Migration Amendment (Preventing Further Stay for Visitor Visas) Regulations 2026, signed by Governor-General Sam Mostyn on November 12, 2026, under the Migration Act 1958.
Full list: Malaysia drops 20 African countries from visa-free entry
The regulations amend the existing Migration Regulations 1994.
PAY ATTENTION: TUKO is in WhatsApp Channels now! Subscribe and read news in your favourite messenger.
The amendment makes Condition 8503, known as the "No Further Stay" condition, mandatory across three visitor visa categories:
Previously, the condition applied automatically to some Subclass 600 streams but could be applied at the immigration minister's discretion in others.
The new regulations remove that flexibility and standardise the restriction across all three visa types.
Under Condition 8503, a visitor generally cannot lodge a valid onshore application for any other substantive visa, with the exception of a protection visa, unless the minister grants a waiver.

The explanatory statement accompanying the regulations confirms this, stating that the condition "provides that the holder will not, after entering Australia, be entitled to be granted a substantive visa, other than a protection visa, while the holder remains in Australia."
Canada to offer 5,500 slots to foreign workers by making rural programme permanent
This effectively closes the door on visitors attempting to transition onshore to employer-sponsored, student, partner or skilled migration pathways after arrival.
The Australian Government says the amendments are designed to ensure visitor visas serve their intended purpose: facilitating short-term stays.
The changes aim to "facilitate short-term visits and limit onshore visa hopping and pathways that facilitate extended onshore residence."

The government also expects the regulations to contribute to managing overall migration levels and reducing net overseas migration, while discouraging non-genuine applicants from using visitor visas as a gateway to successive temporary visa applications.
The new conditions apply only to applications lodged on or after November 28, 2026.
People who already hold valid visitor visas will not be retrospectively affected, nor will applicants who submit their applications before the commencement date.
The government confirmed it will retain the power to waive Condition 8503 in qualifying circumstances under the existing provisions of subregulation 2.05 of the Migration Regulations.
Waivers are not automatic and must be applied for individually.
UK Embassy Kenya announces deadline to apply for 2027 fully funded Commonwealth scholarships
Foreign nationals planning to visit Australia are advised to determine their intended immigration pathway before travelling.

Those considering employment, education or long-term residence in Australia should pursue the appropriate visa category from outside the country rather than assuming they can make the switch after arrival.

In other news, Australia will introduce stricter assessments of Bridging Visa B (BVB) applications linked to employer-sponsored visa pathways from November 30 , 2026, requiring foreign workers to provide stronger evidence that overseas travel is necessary.

The changes affect applicants awaiting decisions on Skills in Demand (Subclass 482), Employer Nomination Scheme (Subclass 186) and Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Subclass 494) visas, as well as their included family members.

Applicants will need to provide specific travel dates, itineraries and supporting documents such as medical records, business invitations or evidence of family events, with general holiday or family visit explanations potentially insufficient on their own.
The BVB application fee stands at AUD 575 (approximately KSh 48,000), while applications lodged before November 30 will continue under the existing assessment approach.

items.title: Cheruiyot boosts Kisumu West traders, says small businesses drive grassroots economy
items.description: Senate Majority Leader Aaron Cheruiyot joined traders in Kisumu West, Kisumu, at the invitation of Hon. Rozzah Buyu, to recognise and boost smallholder
content: Senate Majority Leader Aaron Cheruiyot joined traders in Kisumu West, Kisumu, at the invitation of Hon. Rozzah Buyu, to recognise and boost smallholder traders.Cheruiyot described traders, in all their diverse crafts, as the most effective drivers of the economy at the grassroots.

He said traders work tirelessly and devise innovative strategies to navigate the complexities and overcome the challenges of the business world, often with little support but with great determination.
To recognise their hard work, the leaders boosted the businesses of smallholder traders in the constituency, offering encouragement and support to help them grow.

Speaking at the event, Cheruiyot said the initiative was guided by the Usawa Agenda, which seeks to uplift every Kenyan to lead a decent life and build a nation where everyone is valued and appreciated.
He said the agenda is about fairness, dignity and equal opportunity, ensuring that no Kenyan, however small their business, is left behind.

Cheruiyot thanked the people of Kisumu for their overwhelming support for the Broad-Based Government and for their decision to grant President William Samoei Ruto another mandate to strengthen national unity and implement progressive policies for all Kenyans.
He said the support shown in Kisumu was a sign of growing trust in the government’s agenda of inclusion, economic empowerment and national cohesion.
The event brought together traders from different sectors, who shared their experiences and aspirations, with leaders pledging continued support to strengthen grassroots enterprises.

items.title: Nairobi runs on borrowed money: CoB flags Sidian Bank overdraft averaging KSh1.6B a month
items.description: Nairobi County has been maintaining a monthly overdraft facility with Sidian Bank of Kenya averaging KSh1.6B to cover staff salaries, with an outstanding balance of KSh1.54B recorded as at 31 March 2026, the Controller of Budget has flagged in a report raising fresh concerns about the county's chronic dependence on short-term borrowing to meet its most basic financial obligations.
content: Nairobi County is financing its monthly wage bill through a rolling bank overdraft — and the Controller of Budget says the arrangement has cost taxpayers millions in charges and penalties.

Nairobi County has been maintaining a monthly overdraft facility with Sidian Bank of Kenya averaging KSh1.6B to cover staff salaries, with an outstanding balance of KSh1.54B recorded as at 31 March 2026, the Controller of Budget has flagged in a report raising fresh concerns about the county’s chronic dependence on short-term borrowing to meet its most basic financial obligations.

Controller of Budget Margaret Nyakang’o’s report reveals that the County Executive has relied on the Sidian Bank overdraft facility specifically to cover personnel emoluments, with the outstanding balance standing at KSh1.54B by 31 March 2026. The county also carried an additional overdraft of KSh214.51M with Co-operative Bank.

Nyakang’o confirmed the arrangement before the Senate Standing Committee on Information Communication and Technology on Monday, noting that the commercial bank had confirmed the facility enabled the county to settle salary payments up to October 2026. She further recommended integrating gratuity into the payroll system and ensuring timely submission of monthly salary requisitions — basic financial hygiene that the county has consistently struggled to maintain.

Beyond the overdrafts, Nairobi still carries a long-standing KSh4.5B loan from Kenya Commercial Bank secured in 2010 under the defunct Nairobi City Council, which remains classified under trade payables — a debt so old it predates devolution, yet one that continues to weigh on a county that spent KSh32.12B on development and recurrent programmes in the reporting period, representing 136 per cent of funds actually released by the Controller of Budget.

That a city generating billions in revenue each year cannot pay its workers without a rolling commercial overdraft is not a fiscal footnote. It is an indictment — and with Nairobi’s 2027 election politics already heating up, the question of who bears responsibility for the financial mess at City Hall is about to become very uncomfortable for everyone inside it.

items.title: Real Madrid vs Celta Vigo La Liga prediction: Match preview, team news, current form & h2h
items.description: Heavyweights Real Madrid return to La Liga action looking to maintain their excellent run of form when they host Celta Vigo on Saturday evening.
content: Heavyweights Real Madrid return to La Liga action looking to maintain their excellent run of form when they host Celta Vigo on Saturday evening.
Madrid are second in the table with 30 points from 12 matches, three points behind leaders Barcelona.
They have won 10 of their 12 league matches, scoring 31 goals and conceding only 10 prior to this much anticipated encounter.
Celta, meanwhile, sit 11th with 13 points, having won only two of their 12 league matches.
Their biggest problem has been at the attacking end: they have scored just 10 goals so far, although they have also conceded only 10.
Jose Mourinho’s side come into the game on an impressive eight-game winning streak, scoring 24 goals in the process.
Their opponents have won just one of their last five games and all the pressure lies on them as they seek only a second win against Madrid in their last 26 attempts.
At the Bernabéu, their form has been even more impressive. They have won their last five home league matches and are yet to drop a league point at home this season.
Here is our predicted outcome for the match.
The match kicks off at 11PM E.A.T at the Santiago Bernabeau
ALSO READ: SportPesa League round eight weekend predictions: Match previews, team news, current form & h2h
The biggest news for the hosts is the return of Vinícius Junior, who has completed his domestic suspension.
His return is particularly significant because Madrid have still managed to win consistently without him, but his individual ability gives the team another elite attacking weapon.
The latest squad announcement confirms that Kylian Mbappé will lead the attacking line, supported by Jude Bellingham and Arda Güler.
Aurelien Tchouameni and Bernardo Silva are also in training and are fighting for a place in the starting XI.
Borja Iglesas is the latest on the Celta injury lost and joins Miguel Roman and Alvaro Nunez on the sidelines.
Other than that, the rest of the side is fit and will be led by Oscar Mingueza and Jonathan Bamba in the final third.
Madrid have dominated the overall rivalry. Across the most recent 10 meetings, Madrid have won nine, with Celta winning one.
The rare win came in a shock 2-0 victory last December at the Bernabeau, and they are hoping to replicate that success here.
Madrid are unbeaten at home in the league, have won their last five home league matches and have won eight straight games in all competitions.
Celta’s away record makes the task even more difficult.
Madrid have scored 31 goals in 12 league matches, while Celta have scored only 10. The home side have also scored at least twice in several of their recent victories.
Prediction – Real Madrid to win and/or Over 2.5 goals

"One day at a time": Baba Talisha undergoes transplant to save his left eye
items.description: Baba Talisha undergoes urgent cornea transplant in Kenya to save his left eye after a severe infection caused perforation, as he seeks funds for care abroad.
content: PAY ATTENTION: TUKO is in WhatsApp Channels now! Subscribe and read news in your favourite messenger.

Kenyan influencer Baba Talisha shared a deeply personal update on Saturday, November 21, 2026, revealing he was undergoing a cornea transplant at a hospital in Kenya in a bid to save his remaining good eye.

In the post shared on Instagram , Baba Talisha disclosed that an aggressive infection, one that doctors have struggled to identify and bring under control, had caused his cornea to perforate, forcing his medical team to recommend the surgery as an urgent intervention.
Kibabii University graduate who sold scrap metal to support family, pay fees, shares touching story
The influencer's health struggles have been unfolding publicly over recent weeks.
PAY ATTENTION: TUKO is in WhatsApp Channels now! Subscribe and read news in your favourite messenger.
He had previously revealed that he lost the ability to see in his right eye, a development that sent shockwaves through his online following.
Now, with pressure in his right eye remaining dangerously high despite medical efforts to lower it, and with his left cornea perforated, the situation has taken a more critical turn.

His doctors advised that the transplant was necessary not only to protect his left eye but also to stabilise his condition ahead of a planned trip to India, where he is expected to undergo further investigations and access more specialised care.
Mungai Eve opens up about hair transplant to restore her hairline
Baba Talisha has also reached out to Kenyans to support him financially as the cost of treatment both locally and abroad continues to mount.
Despite the weight of the situation, the influencer struck a hopeful tone in his message, saying he was taking the journey "one day at a time, with hope and gratitude for everyone walking beside us."

The post, which was shared while wearing what appeared to be an LCIF Lions Clubs International Foundation SightFirst-branded item, also hinted at more details to come, with the caption cutting off mid-sentence, leaving followers eager for his next update.

Baba Talisha's wife, Miss Wanjey, recently revealed during a TikTok livestream that a parasitic amoeba linked to contaminated water and dust embedded in Baba Talisha's cornea caused total vision loss in his eye.
She noted that they were awaiting lab results sent to India before starting new treatment, planning a second opinion at Kikuyu Hospital, and considering a corneal transplant if medication fails.
While hoping he regains most of his sight, Miss Wanjey stepped in to manage his business communications as he deals with light sensitivity and recovery.

Uganda tightens Ebola controls in 34 DRC border districts
items.description: The rules cover gatherings, returning travellers, aid workers and public facilities, while Kenya’s outbreak remains linked to one reported cluster.
content: The rules cover gatherings, returning travellers, aid workers and public facilities, while Kenya’s outbreak remains linked to one reported cluster.

Uganda has tightened controls in 34 high-risk districts bordering the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), requiring health ministry clearance for mass gatherings and 21 days of quarantine or monitored self-isolation for Ugandans returning from the DRC. The measures took effect immediately and are intended to reduce the risk of Ebola crossing the border.

The restrictions were set out in a public health advisory on November 19 by Ministry of Health Permanent Secretary Diana Atwine. Both Capital FM and The Star reported that Uganda’s National Task Force on Epidemic Preparedness and Response approved the measures after assessing the risk from the outbreak in the DRC. Atwine said authorities had seen continued movement across the border, including through unofficial crossing points. She also said earlier restrictions remain in force.

In the designated districts, local authorities are to monitor new arrivals and people moving into communities. Local Council chairpersons must be notified of those movements. People who cross illegally, and those who help them, may face legal action.

The gathering rule is more specific than a blanket ban. Concerts, festivals, political rallies and similar events cannot proceed in the districts without written clearance from the Ministry of Health. The Star’s headline describes the events as suspended, while its report, like Capital FM’s, says they require prior approval. Neither account says all gatherings have been prohibited outright.

Returning Ugandans must undergo health risk assessments before quarantine or monitored self-isolation. Humanitarian workers need clearance from the Director General of Health Services to cross the border, and moving bodies into or out of Uganda also requires government authorisation. Day scholars travelling between the two countries in the designated districts are barred from crossing; boarding students with possible exposure must complete 21 days in designated quarantine facilities before returning to school.

Airports, accommodation and public facilities are also covered. Entebbe International Airport has enhanced screening for arriving and departing passengers, and travellers must complete locator forms before boarding. Airlines and other transport operators risk sanctions if they knowingly carry people without proper authorisation or documentation. Hotels must keep guest registers and verify identification. Schools, health facilities, transport terminals, places of worship and other public facilities must provide handwashing facilities and follow infection-prevention measures. Radio stations in the affected districts must devote at least two hours a month to Ebola-prevention campaigns.

The accounts largely agree on the scope and terms of the restrictions. Capital FM gives extra detail on the instructions to local leaders and the monitoring of hotels and schools. The Star supplies the clearest account of the Kenyan outbreak: it reports that the first case was confirmed on October 6, after a traveller came through Uganda from the DRC; the patient died in Nairobi on October 5. The Star says Kenya recorded nine cases and two deaths , all linked to one transmission cluster, with no evidence of community transmission.

Capital FM says Kenya was approaching the end of its Ebola monitoring period, but the report provided cuts off before giving an end date or further details. The Star does not give a monitoring-period deadline. That leaves the status and timing of the end of monitoring unclear in these accounts.

Only two outlets in this coverage have reported the new measures, so the available reporting is narrow. Both describe an extensive set of controls, but neither says how long they will remain in force or how compliance will be enforced beyond the stated penalties and sanctions. Those details, and whether the rules will prevent further cross-border transmission, are still open.

items.title: Alcohol Use Among Young People Raises Public Health Concerns in Kenya
items.description: By Melisa Mong’ina   Nairobi, Kenya: Alcohol intake among young adults is raising public health concerns in the country, with university students
content: Nairobi, Kenya: Alcohol intake among young adults is raising public health concerns in the country, with university students recording higher levels of consumption and addiction than the general population.

A 2024 study by the National Authority for the Campaign Against Alcohol and Drug Abuse (NACADA) found that alcohol use was higher among university students, at 18.6%, compared with 3.8% among secondary school students and 2.6% among primary school pupils. The study also found that 8.7% of university students had severe alcohol use disorder.

Speaking during a virtual discussion on alcohol control legislation organised by NCD Alliance Kenya, NACADA, Students Campaign Against Drugs (SCAD) and the International Institute for Legislative Affairs (IILA), Adrian Njenga of NACADA warned that early exposure to alcohol could increase the risk of addiction and the use of other substances.
“Alcohol and tobacco are referred to as the gatekeepers or the initiators into the drug world for young people,” said Njenga.

Dr. Catherine Karekezi from NCD Alliance Kenya highlighted that alcohol is a major risk factor for non-communicable diseases, including heart conditions and certain cancers, as well as mental health problems.

“Alcohol is toxic. It is a psychoactive agent. It is a dependence-producing substance that has been classified as a Group One carcinogen by the International Agency for Research on Cancer,” Dr. Karekezi said.
She also warned about the effects of alcohol on young people, saying their developing brains make them particularly vulnerable to its long-term effects.
“If we have adolescents and young adults exposed to alcohol consumption, this increases the likelihood of dependency on alcohol,” she added.
Dr. Karekezi underscored that alcohol dependence can also push Kenyan households into poverty, affecting families and the country’s economic development.

Benjamin Odhiambo, a public health expert at the Students Campaign Against Drugs (SCAD) also supported raising the minimum drinking age to 21, arguing that delaying exposure to alcohol could reduce the risk of addiction.
“The earlier an individual is introduced or initiated into substance use, the more likely they are to graduate into problematic alcohol use and then alcohol use disorder,” he said.
Odhiambo added that raising the legal age for drinking and handling alcohol would help protect young people.

He also raised concerns about young people’s exposure to alcohol advertising on social media platforms, stressing that stronger controls on advertising and better tracking of alcoholic products could help protect them and other consumers.
“This shows that we do not have sufficient protections for young people in terms of exposure to these particular products, especially alcohol,” said Odhiambo.

According to Caleb Mbugua of the International Institute for Legislative Affairs (IILA), the proposed Alcoholic Drinks and Drugs Control Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeks to raise the minimum legal drinking age from 18 to 21 to protect the health of young people.
He explained that the proposed changes would also prevent people below the new legal age from obtaining alcohol licences or working in places where alcoholic drinks are sold or handled.

The bill would also restrict their access to areas where alcohol is manufactured, stored or consumed, and prohibit the sale of alcoholic drinks to them or to anyone accompanied by people below the new legal age.
“There will be warning signs and notices reflecting the new age limit and alcohol outlets will not be allowed to admit underage customers, whether they are alone or accompanied,” said Mbugua.
